title: Strong L2 compactness through possible contact for vanishing structural viscosity in periodic two-dimensional fluid–beam systems
author: Jean-Jérôme Casanova; Céline Grandmont; Matthieu Hillairet
work: On an existence theory for a fluid-beam problem encompassing possible contacts
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.162
difficulty_reason: The ordinary Aubin–Lions lemma does not apply directly to velocities on unknown moving domains when the limiting beam can contact the cavity bottom. The authors construct a source-specific lower interface and prove continuity of fractional-domain projections with the full cofactor/streamfunction construction, allowing projected time-derivative compactness on fixed domains. Their complete approximation-error and energy-pairing argument then gives strong fluid/beam velocity convergence through possible contact, rather than leaving the new contact geometry or projection closure to a reference.
